fichas.title: Natural stone floor slabs
fichas.summary: Natural stone slabs of limestone, slate, and sandstone may retain their naturally split roughness or be partly or fully sanded. Sawn slabs, including limestone (marble), sandstone, and volcanic stone, can receive specified surface treatments. Slabs are laid in a mortar bed or glued to screed. The page illustrates irregular crazy paving and slabs laid in Roman bonding.
figure_refs: 1 Irregular laying of natural stone (crazy paving)
2 Natural stone slabs in Roman bonding

fichas.title: Mosaic flooring
fichas.summary: Mosaic flooring made from glass, ceramic, or natural stone is laid in a mortar bed or glued. The page depicts square and hexagonal mosaics, circular cut-outs, five-sided pieces, an Essen pattern, and square layouts with smaller inserts.

fichas.title: Ceramic floor tiles
fichas.summary: Stoneware and mosaic floor tiles are made from clay and sintered during firing, so they absorb almost no water. The text describes them as frost-resistant, somewhat acid-resistant, subject to little mechanical wear, and not resistant to oil.

fichas.title: Floor tile modular systems and laying patterns
fichas.summary: Diagrams show modular systems for stoneware and split tiles, with module subdivisions, and a variety of floor-laying patterns. Patterns include basket and weave layouts, herringbone, ship deck, English, ladder, Burgundy, and cube patterns, several shown with friezes.
